<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

adjacent(R0,C0,R,C) :- delta(DR,DC), R = R0+DR, C = C0+DC.

rowMin := #min{R1 : wallCell(R1,C1), maxDist(R1,C1) = bestDist, C1 = colMin}.

% Determine grid dimensions
maxRow = #max{R : input(R,_,_)}.
maxCol = #max{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

adjacent(R0,C0,R,C) :- delta(DR,DC), R = R0+DR, C = C0+DC.

% reachable from border through non-wall cells (wall value 2)
borderReachable(R,C) :- R = 0, input(R,C,X), X != 2.
borderReachable(R,C) :- R = maxRow, input(R,C,X), X != 2.
borderReachable(R,C) :- C = 0, input(R,C,X), X != 2.
borderReachable(R,C) :- C = maxCol, input(R,C,X), X != 2.

reachable(R,C) :- borderReachable(R,C).
reachable(R,C) :- reachable(R0,C0), delta(DR,DC), R = R0+DR, C = C0+DC, input(R,C,X), X != 2.

% interior zeros (hole cells)
interiorZeros(R,C) :- input(R,C,0), not reachable(R,C).

% wall cells that touch interior zeros
wallCell(R,C) :- input(R,C,2), interiorZeros(R0,C0), adjacent(R0,C0,R,C).

% at least two interior zeros
multipleInterior :- interiorZeros(R1,C1), interiorZeros(R2,C2), R1 != R2, C1 != C2.

% farthest wall cell for single interior case
maxDist(R,C) :- #max{D : D = R; D = maxRow - R; D = C; D = maxCol - C}.

bestDist := #max{D : wallCell(R1,C1), maxDist(R1,C1) = D}.
colMin := #min{C1 : wallCell(R1,C1), maxDist(R1,C1) = bestDist}.
rowMin := #min{R1 : wallCell(R1,C1), maxDist(R1,C1) = bestDist, C1 = colMin}.

selectedWall(R,C) :- wallCell(R,C), maxDist(R,C) = bestDist, C = colMin, R = rowMin.

% each cell must have exactly one colour
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

1 { output(R,C,Actual) : color(Actual) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% transformation rules
% interior holes become colour 3
:- interiorZeros(R,C), output(R,C,Actual), Actual != 3.

% walls that surround interior (multiple interior) become 0
:- wallCell(R,C), multipleInterior, output(R,C,Actual), Actual != 0.

% single interior: the selected wall becomes 3, others become 0
:- wallCell(R,C), not multipleInterior, selectedWall(R,C), output(R,C,Actual), Actual != 3.
:- wallCell(R,C), not multipleInterior, not selectedWall(R,C), output(R,C,Actual), Actual != 0.

% regular cells keep their original colour
:- input(R,C,V), not interiorZeros(R,C), not wallCell(R,C), output(R,C,Actual), color(Actual), Actual != V.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Grid dimensions
maxRow(R) :- R = #max{R : input(R,_,_)}.
nRows(N)  :- N = maxRow + 1.
maxCol(C) :- C = #max{C : input(_,C,_)}.
nCols(M)  :- M = maxCol + 1.

% Neighbourhood
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).
adjacent(R0,C0,R,C) :- delta(DR,DC), R = R0+DR, C = C0+DC.

% Wall value
wallVal = 2.

% Cells reachable from the border through non‑wall cells
borderReachable(R,C) :- R = 0,    input(R,C,X), X != wallVal.
borderReachable(R,C) :- R = nRows-1,input(R,C,X), X != wallVal.
borderReachable(R,C) :- C = 0,    input(R,C,X), X != wallVal.
borderReachable(R,C) :- C = nCols-1,input(R,C,X), X != wallVal.

reachable(R,C) :- borderReachable(R,C).
reachable(R,C) :- reachable(R0,C0), adjacent(R0,C0,R,C), input(R,C,X), X != wallVal.

% Interior holes (zeros not reachable from the border)
interiorZeros(R,C) :- input(R,C,0), not reachable(R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------
% Count interior zeros and derive case flags
countI(K)  :- K = #count{R : interiorZeros(R,_)}.

singleI    :- countI(1).                       % exactly one interior zero
hasMultipleI :- countI(K), K > 1.             % at least two interior zeros

% Column and row counts of interior zeros
colCount(Kc) :- Kc = #count{C : interiorZeros(_ , C)}.
rowCount(Kr) :- Kr = #count{R : interiorZeros(R,_)}.

colCountOne   :- colCount(Kc), Kc = 1.
colCountMore  :- colCount(Kc), Kc > 1.
rowCountMore  :- rowCount(Kr), Kr > 1.

% Specific patterns
verticalLineCase :- hasMultipleI, colCountOne, rowCountMore.   % interior zeros in a single column (vertical line)
rectCase       :- hasMultipleI, colCountMore, rowCountMore.    % interior zeros form a genuine region (at least 2 rows and 2 cols)

% -------------------------------------------------
% Adjacent walls and left‑side walls for the vertical line
wall(R,C)          :- input(R,C,w), w = wallVal.
adj_wall(R,C)      :- wall(R0,C0), adjacent(R0,C0,R,C), interiorZeros(R,C).

adj_left(R,C)      :- interiorZeros(Ir,Jc), wall(R,C), R = Ir, C = Jc - 1.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Output colours

% 1) Single interior zero (the hole is a single cell)
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    singleI, interiorZeros(R,C), Actual = 3.
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    singleI, adj_wall(R,C), Actual = 0.
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    singleI, wall(R,C),   Actual = 0.

% 2) Region case (multiple interior zeros forming an area)
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    rectCase, interiorZeros(R,C), Actual = 3.
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    rectCase, adj_wall(R,C), Actual = 0.
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    rectCase, wall(R,C),   Actual = 0.

output(R,C,Actual) :-
    verticalLineCase, interiorZeros(R,C), Actual = 0.
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    verticalLineCase, adj_wall(R,C), not adj_left(R,C), Actual = 0.
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    verticalLineCase, adj_left(R,C), Actual = 3.
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    verticalLineCase, wall(R,C), not adj_wall(R,C), Actual = 0.

output(R,C,Actual) :-

    not rectCase,

    wall(R,C),

% 5) Keep original colour for all other cells
output(R,C,Actual) :-
    input(R,C,V), not interiorZeros(R,C), not wall(R,C), Actual = V.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Ensure each cell gets exactly one colour
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

singleI    :- countI(1).                       % exactly one interior zero
hasMultipleI :- countI(K), K > 1.             % at least two interior zeros

% Column and row counts of interior zeros
colCount(Kc) :- Kc = #count{C : interiorZeros(_ , C)}.
rowCount(Kr) :- Kr = #count{R : interiorZeros(R,_)}.

colCountOne   :- colCount(Kc), Kc = 1.
colCountMore  :- colCount(Kc), Kc > 1.
rowCountMore  :- rowCount(Kr), Kr > 1.

% Specific patterns
verticalLineCase :- hasMultipleI, colCountOne, rowCountMore.   % interior zeros in a single column (vertical line)
rectCase       :- hasMultipleI, colCountMore, rowCountMore.    % interior zeros form a genuine region (at least 2 rows and 2 cols)

% Adjacent walls and left‑side walls for the vertical line
wall(R,C)          :- input(R,C,w), w = wallVal.
adj_wall(R,C)      :- wall(R0,C0), adjacent(R0,C0,R,C), interiorZeros(R,C).

adj_left(R,C)      :- interiorZeros(Ir,Jc), wall(R,C), R = Ir, C = Jc - 1.
